title: Stratified promptset specification and sequential rollback policy for Optimize evals
creator: Aisha Reddy
body:
Overview:
This PRD defines the promptset stratification, sampling matrix, Signal/metric definitions, statistical testing approach, A/B gating thresholds, and a sequential rollback policy for Optimize eval rollouts. The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable acceptance gates that balance sensitivity to regressions with robustness to noise and long-tail variance.

Goals:
- Create a reusable promptset spec (schema + cohorts) for Optimize that supports: cohort-level and aggregate evaluation, stratified sampling, and progressive canaries.
- Define numeric regression thresholds and multi-signal rollback rules that are actionable for runtime rollouts (hosted and dedicated).
- Standardize A/B test requirements (min sample, MDE, alpha/power) and sequential stopping rules compatible with streaming telemetry.
- Provide operational runbook: detection windows, alerting, rollback automation boundaries, and postmortem checklist.

Non-goals:
- Changes to model training or offline eval tooling beyond the import/export format.
- A bespoke UI for promptset editing (we will integrate with existing Optimize console endpoints).

Promptset specification (format):
- Required fields per example: prompt_id, cohort_tag, input_text, completion_reference, task_type (chat|completion|classification|ranking), metadata.labels (list), expected_behavior_notes, sensitivity_level (low|medium|high).
- Cohorts: customer-facing, safety-sensitive, edgecases, high-cost (long outputs), short-turn (<=64 tokens), long-turn (>512 tokens), embeddings, reranker_testset.
- For each cohort include: desired sample_size (see sampling matrix), stratification keys (region, device_type, language), and priority (critical|recommended|optional).

Sampling matrix and sizes (minimums):
- Aggregate baseline: 5k examples across all cohorts per model candidate.
- Safety-sensitive cohort: 2k examples, stratified by language and region.
- Long-tail / edgecases: 1k examples per cohort with oversampling of rare classes up to 10x relative to baseline prevalence.
- Embeddings/reranker: 3k paired examples.
- Canary-level small sample for fast rollouts: 500 examples (must be used only for signal detection, not final decision unless combined with traffic-level metrics).
- For A/B live tests the minimum per-arm sample is 10k user requests or 72 hours active traffic, whichever comes first, unless the model has clear signal from canary cohorts (see gating rules).

Signal & metric definitions (primary + supporting):
- Primary quality signal: weighted composite QualityScore computed per-example: QualityScore = 0.6 * automated_semantic_score + 0.3 * human_rating_normalized + 0.1 * safety_flag_score. Each subcomponent range-normalized to [0,1].
- Preference/utility metrics: completion_latency_ms (p95), tokens_per_response, effective_token_cost_per_response.
- Business/guardrail metrics: downstream_conversion_rate (customer metric), error_rate (API errors %), safety_violations_per_1k.
- Cohort quantile metrics: q10, q50, q90 of QualityScore per cohort for long-tail detection.

Statistical testing and thresholds:
- Default hypothesis testing: two-sided bootstrap for QualityScore median with 95% CI. For A/B decisions use permutation tests with alpha=0.01 and target power=0.8 for MDE=2.5 percentage points on QualityScore.
- Regression threshold (statistical): a model candidate is flagged if the lower bound of the 95% CI for delta(QualityScore) relative to baseline is < -1.5 points AND effect is seen in >=2 priority cohorts.
- Practical threshold (business): immediate hold if composite QualityScore drops >=3 points on customer-facing cohort OR safety_violations increase >50% absolute vs baseline and exceed 1 per 1k.
- Latency/cost fallback thresholds: p95 latency increase >50ms AND cost per response >10% over baseline triggers canary throttling.

A/B gating rules (live traffic):
- Stage 1: Canary (1% traffic, 24h) — collect canary cohorts and runtime metrics. If any practical threshold breach -> immediate rollback.
- Stage 2: Expanded canary (10% traffic, 72h) — requires statistical test: no significant negative delta by permutation test (alpha=0.01). If test inconclusive but no practical threshold breach, escalate to manual review.
- Stage 3: Full rollout (100%) — requires passing both statistical and practical checks across priority cohorts and passing operational health checks (errors, latency, cost).
- Sequential testing note: allow alpha spending using O'Brien-Fleming-like schedule to avoid inflated false positives during multiple interim analyses. Maintain audit log of interim p-values.

Rollback policy (sequential & asymmetric):
- Rollback triggers (automated):
  - Any safety_violations_per_1k > 1.0 (automatic abort and rollback).
  - Composite QualityScore drop >=3 points on customer-facing or safety-sensitive cohorts sustained for two consecutive detection windows (24h windows).
  - p95 latency degradation >2x or >500ms absolute.
- Rollback escalation (manual):
  - Statistical flag only (e.g., lower CI breach but no practical impact) -> create urgent review, hold traffic ramp, do not rollback automatically unless coincident business metric deterioration (conversion, retention) observed.
  - Persistent small regressions (1.5–3 points) across 4 consecutive windows -> auto-throttle to 10% and notify PM/SE/ops; auto-rollback if not remediated in 48h.
- Safe fallback: maintain last-known-good model variant in routing; rollback should be revertible with WAF-style staged traffic return with health checks.

Monitoring, alerts and dashboards:
- Dashboards required: per-cohort QualityScore distribution (q10/50/90), delta vs baseline in real-time, latency/cost heatmaps, safety violation trends, traffic split charts for canaries.
- Alerts: Critical (pager) for automated rollback triggers; High (email + slack) for statistical flags; Medium for gradual drift (weekly digest).
- Retention: store per-example eval history for 90 days; aggregate rollup data for 3 years for audit/compliance.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before ship to customers):
- PRD approved by engineering and research (signoffs captured).
- Promptset schema documented and validated by 3 example imports from customer-simulated datasets.
- Sampling matrix implemented in Optimize import/export and unit-tested (coverage >= 90%).
- Statistical test library integrated with Optimize eval pipelines and validated on synthetic regressions (benchmarks showing Type I rate <= alpha target).
- Canary automation implemented with clear escalation paths; end-to-end smoke test that simulates a safety regression and validates automated rollback.
- Console indicators for pass/fail and links to failing prompt examples in the runbook.

Operational runbook highlights (short):
- Detection windows: default 24h sliding window with optional 6h sub-windows for high-sensitivity cohorts.
- Escalation matrix: SRE on-call -> PM -> Research lead -> Legal (if safety/legal flagged).
- Postmortem timeframe: 72 hours to publish initial incident summary; 7 days for full impact analysis and remediation plan.

QA & Validation plan:
- Synthetic regression injection tests across cohorts (automated daily): inject -2/ -4/ -6 point deltas and assert rollback/alerts behavior.
- Load tests for canary automation under 10k RPS to validate throttling and routing.
- Human rating panel: 200 examples per major cohort evaluated each model candidate for the first two months of rollout.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require human rating for every candidate for first 30 days? (Cost vs safety tradeoff).
- How aggressively should we spend alpha across interim analyses? Proposed: O'Brien-Fleming with 3 interim looks.
- Should safety_violations threshold be an absolute number or dynamically scaled by baseline prevalence?

expected_outcomes: Faster, safer rollouts with repeatable, auditable decisioning; fewer false-positive rollbacks and clearer escalation paths for borderline statistical flags.
